svg.text: First design, for review before any code: how a person starts a presentation, what the audience sees, what the presenter sees, and the few states in between. Questions 1–5 were answered on 2026-11-13; the timing screen (G) is a new proposal.
A · Starting: View menu and the Present button
Present is a View entry (the suite has no Slide Show menu) plus one apricot
button at the bar's right end. Every entry has a key; F5 follows convention.
“Speaker notes” shows the notes field under the canvas (B).
“Present with presenter view” opens the audience window and turns
this one into the presenter view (C). Plain “Present” shows only D.
B · Editing: speaker notes under the canvas
One Markdown field per slide, in the document, undoable, attributed like any edit; shown formatted in the presenter view only. Never on the slide or the slide print page. The
AI may write it. Next to it: the planned time (⏱); the rail shows each slide's time and the total.
Start from the 2019 baseline, not from today.
**Pause:** ask which bar they expect to be largest.
tobi moved text box on slide 3
C · The presenter view (this window, on the presenter's own screen)
What the audience cannot see: next slide, Markdown notes, time against the plan. Dark Ink surface so it does not light up the room; notes at reading size.
The audience window shows only D. Both follow the same slide; going forward in either window moves both.
← → Space · B blank · G overview · number + Enter
Start from the 2019 baseline, not from today.
ask the room which bar they expect to be largest.
• Then reveal it: heating falls first
Markdown, shown formatted. Raw HTML and images are not shown. ± changes the text size.
Slide only, letterboxed on Ink, no chrome, cursor hidden.
Controls fade in on mouse move and out after 2 s.
Transitions: none by default; one quiet fade (150 ms) as the only choice,
switched off by prefers-reduced-motion. No builds in the first version.
Slide is drawn once, scaled to fit (1600×900 space, D83), not re-laid-out.
G, or a click on the counter. Arrow keys move, Enter goes, Esc returns.
Typing a number and Enter works without opening it.
Once templates exist, a tile names its template (E10.5):
never unsure where a slide comes from.
Badges show the planned time; a slide without one shows “–”
and counts as 0:00. Planned total 18:30 across 12 slides.
Kept deliberately few. Each is one key and one key back.
After the last slide, once; then
Audience view; notes stay hidden. P swaps
to the presenter view in the same window.
One line in the People list, like any
other presence; nothing in the document.
Not in the first version: pointer or laser, ink on slides, builds, audience Q&A, remote
viewers, recording, a notes page in print (D917 keeps room for the layout).
G · Planning the time: per slide, and the whole talk
A planned time per slide is stored in the document next to the notes (one command, undoable). The total is always in view; nothing is enforced and nobody has to plan.
T opens this. Type 2 and Enter for two minutes;
m:ss works too. Opened from ⏱ in the notes field
or from a slide's context menu.
“Available time” is an optional line of the document's metadata (D71):
set it, or leave it. The total is shown in the rail (B), the overview (E)
After the show · presenter view only
Kept in this browser only until closed.
